audit_note: 2026-10-19 clean session (results/clean_final/) resolved the TTFT issues: (1) TTFT p50 depends on request count (32req vs 128req changes p50 2.6x at c32) - Cline compared across request counts without noticing; (2) two-server imbalance was a client-side artifact, clean per-server measurement is balanced (<2%); (3) cross-day node differences add ~2x residual on TTFT at c>=8. Throughput verdicts were always reliable. Use clean_session_2026_10_19 numbers for any latency comparison.

EP.desc: --enable-expert-parallel already in all server configs. Distributes 256 experts across TP ranks (32/card with TP8). Not a separate topology.

speedup.note: 27% throughput gain for 2x cards. TTFT worse because each server independently queues 64 concurrent requests.

low_latency.reason: Single-request TTFT ~350ms. DP does not improve this.

best_overall.reason: Sub-linear 16-card scaling. Better to serve two different models/services.

key_findings: TP16 infeasible — DeepSeek-V4 architecture cannot shard to 16 TP ranks
DP4xTP4 infeasible — model weights (75 GB/card) exceed 64 GB HBM
vllm-ascend native DP broken on single node (v0.23.0 device assignment bug)
Two independent TP8 servers via ASCEND_RT_VISIBLE_DEVICES is the only working 16-card approach
EP (--enable-expert-parallel) already enabled in all configs, works within each TP8 group
Throughput scaling 8→16 cards is sub-linear (+27%), bottlenecked by prefill
TTFT worsens with 2 servers (each independently queues all concurrent requests)
TPOT robust (45-72ms) across all topologies and concurrencies
NPU 8-15 shows worse TTFT than 0-7 (possible fabric topology asymmetry)
For production: use TP8 on 8 cards, deploy second model on remaining 8 cards
